title: Genes in their domains
summary: A chromosome's protein-coding genes, the 3D domains (TADs) they sit in, what they do and where in the body they are active.

concepts.label: Chromosome
concepts.description: One of the 24 human chromosomes (GRCh38), chosen with the chrom parameter.

children.label: Topologically associating domain
children.description: A stretch of DNA that contacts itself more than its surroundings in Hi-C; domains nest. Called by Arrowhead in one cell line, GM12878.

children.label: Gene
children.description: A protein-coding gene, with its position (start, end in bp).

children.label: Biological process
children.description: UniProt's process keyword, grouped into a system here (the grouping is this board's, not UniProt's).

children.label: Tissue specificity
children.description: HPA's class from RNA in tissues: enriched, group enriched, enhanced, low specificity, not detected.

children.label: RNA expression (nTPM)
children.description: Normalized transcripts per million in a tissue (HPA consensus). RNA, not protein.

children.label: Protein complex
children.description: Proteins that work bound together (curated by Complex Portal, EBI); the gene encodes one subunit. Complexes that differ in one subunit are variants of one family.

children.label: Protein structure
children.description: An experimental 3D structure in the PDB; an entry can hold the whole complex or only some of its subunits.
